title: Silky Pistachio Gelato from Steeped Nut Custard
summary: A luxuriously smooth pistachio gelato with a velvety texture created by steeping ground pistachios in warm milk.
equipment: fine sieve lined with 3 layers of muslin

ingredients.item: shelled unsalted pistachios, plus a few chopped to serve

ingredients.note: 830 ml for the custard base, 60 ml to mix with the cornflour

ingredients.item: glucose syrup or light corn syrup
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind 320 g shelled unsalted pistachios finely in a food processor, about 20 s.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat 830 ml whole milk, 150 g sugar, 80 ml double cream, 80 ml glucose syrup and ¼ tsp fine salt in a large saucepan over medium-high until small bubbles appear at the edge, 5-7 min.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Off heat, stir in the ground pistachios, cover and steep for 1 h.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Strain through a muslin-lined sieve into a bowl, pressing hard. Gather the muslin and squeeze out the remaining liquid; discard the pulp.

steps.title: Custard
steps.text: Mix 13 g cornflour with 60 ml whole milk. Return pistachio milk to the pan, whisk in 5 large egg yolks, and cook over medium, stirring and scraping, until it reaches 88 °C, 4-6 min.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk in the cornflour mixture and stir 30 s until thickened. Pour into a clean bowl, cool 20 min, then chill over iced salted water, stirring, until 4 °C, about 1.5 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Whisk and churn until like thick soft-serve, 15-30 min.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into a container, pressing out air, and freeze until firm, about 6 h.

tips: Strain the mixture through muslin carefully to avoid any gritty particles in the final gelato
Chill the custard mixture to exactly 4 °C before churning for the smoothest result
If the frozen gelato becomes very hard, soften it in the fridge for 1-2 h before scooping
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep frozen in an airtight container; if frozen solid, soften in the fridge for 1-2 h before scooping.
